dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Exhaustively read all source files, identified exact stubbed/buggy functions (exec_numeric stub, exec_load sign-extension bug, missing Call/CallIndirect), reasoned about Br/exec_block control-flow semantics, checked public contract via grep for expect_/imports, and ran a 2/459 baseline before editing — an explicit map of what compiles and what's broken.

Located where 0xFC is decoded to correctly slot in the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode decoding, and studied v128 in spec.rs value parsing (step 19) — orientation on encoding and how v128 integrates with the frozen interface.

Targeted re-research on misbehaving families: decoded actual memory bytes / float bits in python to derive exact trunc_sat and nearest tie-to-even conditions and diagnose load_splat byte-count, rather than guessing semantics.

Probed specific spec-test cases and hex-dumped real wasm binaries (od/xxd), attempted wasm-objdump (unavailable), to disambiguate trap messages, malformed-byte encoding, and lane/alignment questions — orientation continually deepening as new families were reached.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built an explicit, accurate map of the skeleton (stubbed vs buggy functions, value/stack model, decode/runtime/spec wiring, the frozen public API) and pinned non-obvious semantics (sign-extension, trunc_sat bounds, nearest rounding, saturation, trap-message conventions) from the spec and reasoned decoding, fully satisfying the level-8 anchor. It also showed the level-10 behavior of sustained, targeted re-research — decoding bits in python and hex-dumping wasm binaries to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane questions as unfamiliar families appeared. It stops just short of a full 10 only because it never generated wabt reference output to confirm encoding (wasm-objdump was unavailable, so it inspected the provided binaries instead).

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: Laid out a 5-part structure (types enum, SIMD decode, runtime rewrite, validator, spec.rs) — genuine layered decomposition, but organized by code-layer, not by instruction family with spec-test milestones.

Wrote the entire runtime plus ALL SIMD families in one continuous big-bang push (RUNTIME_PART1–12), grouped by shape in the appends but compiled only once at the end — no per-family checkpoint or done-check during implementation. MVP numeric and SIMD were implemented together, not sequenced.
First tests run only after the whole implementation existed (i32.json, block.json, simd_const.json), confirming the single-push rather than milestone-gated approach.

Remaining work was structured by failure CATEGORY (assert_invalid, assert_return, assert_malformed) rather than a family milestone hierarchy; spec_json files were consulted reactively to localize bugs, not as planned family exit-checks.
Late-stage fixes (simd_align, simd_lane, global validation) were driven by which category of failures remained, again showing category-based rather than family-milestone sequencing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed real structure — a 5-component layered plan (step 38) and SIMD code grouped by shape family in the writing — placing it above the 'vague two-phase' anchor (3). But it implemented MVP and all SIMD in a single undifferentiated big-bang push with only one compile, and then debugged by failure category rather than sequencing families each bound to its own spec_json done-check. That falls short of the [5] anchor's 'family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint,' landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: Established a baseline (i32.json 2/459) before making changes, so improvement could be measured against a known starting point.

After implementation ran individual per-family jsons (i32, block, simd_const, call_indirect, memory) and built /tmp/runall.sh aggregate runner; caught that call_indirect/memory crashed (empty output) via per-file inspection.

Repeatedly categorized FAIL lines by assertion type (grep 'FAIL: assert_return/trap/malformed'), isolating the handful of functional failures apart from the mass of assert_invalid, then drilled each to its exact test file/line.

Diagnosed genuine semantic edge cases from individual FAIL lines: trunc saturation boundary (-2147483648.9), and f32.nearest tie-to-even producing -0.0 vs -2.0 — reading expected vs got bit patterns per assertion.
Distinguished an encoding/semantic bug from expectation: load8_splat reading 2 bytes ([0,1] pattern) vs 1, traced to decode/exec rather than assuming test wrong.

When adding the validator, monitored the aggregate and caught MVP regressions ('no current module', block.0.wasm valid module rejected), fixed pop_ctrl before proceeding — guarding MVP while adding validation.

Treated the aggregate pass rate as a monitored signal (95.4%→99.4%→99.8%→99.91%→100%), pursuing exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing', then re-ran the suggested per-family commands and the runner to confirm 34212/34212.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's verification is engineered and self-correcting: it drilled into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (nearest tie-to-even, trunc boundary, sign/-0.0), distinguished real bugs from encoding mismatches (load_splat), guarded against MVP regressions when integrating the validator, and treated the aggregate score as a continuously monitored signal driving toward an exact 1.0 — matching the level-10 description. It falls just short of a pure 10 because the entire SIMD surface was written in one monolithic batch before any test ran, rather than an implement→run-family-json→fix loop per family during construction; the systematic per-family/per-assertion discipline appears mainly in the debugging phase afterward.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: After the big rewrite it immediately establishes an aggregate baseline (2/459→376/459, then 95.4%) and repeatedly categorizes failures with grep -oE 'FAIL: [a-z_]+' | sort | uniq -c, separating assert_invalid vs assert_return vs assert_trap — a running reconciliation of what remains rather than a vague sense.

Tracks the aggregate climbing (95.9%→...) and repeatedly re-runs the full categorization after each fix, working the small set of functional assert_return/trap failures one line at a time (conversions L123, f32.nearest L2505, call_indirect trap msg) and confirming each is gone before moving on — detects and closes individual stuck assertions.

Quantifies the remaining gap concretely (1381 assert_invalid failures dominate) and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining bucket by building a validator, yielding the 99.4% jump — classic effort reallocation to the largest-remaining family.
Catches a regression: the new validator rejects valid modules ('no current module' on block/loop), i.e. a fix in one area broke another; diagnoses block.0.wasm and fixes pop_ctrl, restoring 99.8%.

Maintains a precise shrinking remaining-count ledger to 1.0 across the long tail (69 left → 30 left → 10 global-only → 0), attributing each residual to specific families (simd_align alignment, simd_lane index, global const-expr) and clearing them, never losing the plot.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent continuously reconciles the aggregate score and per-failure-type/per-file counts after nearly every change, quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely (198→69→30→10→0), and reallocates effort to the highest-remaining bucket (the 1381 assert_invalid failures → validator), matching the 8 anchor and reaching into 10 territory. It also detects a fix-induced regression (validator breaking valid block modules) and resolves stuck single assertions individually. It falls short of a full 10 only because progress state is re-derived on demand via grep rather than maintained as an explicit persistent done/remaining/blocked ledger, and SIMD families were never tracked as a written checklist.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Detected load8_splat reading 2 bytes instead of 1 — traced falsified decode/semantic assumption to root and fixed the shape logic rather than patching outputs.

Pivoted from a 'simple heuristic' idea to writing a full validate.rs type-checker after recognizing 1381 assert_invalid failures shared one missing structural cause; single rework flipped ~1381 assertions (376→99.4%).
When the new validator wrongly rejected valid modules, recognized the shared pop_ctrl control-flow helper was the root cause and refactored it once, flipping many tests together (99.4%→99.8%).
Reworked semantic assumptions on trunc trap boundary and nearest tie-to-even after tests falsified them — reconsidering the semantics, not just tweaking numbers.
Some circular re-debugging on undefined vs uninitialized element trap text (flip-flopped), eventually resolved with a general fuzzy match — mild thrashing that keeps it below a 9-10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognized when a failure signaled a structural problem — the missing validator, the buggy shared pop_ctrl helper, wrong lane/decode semantics — and refactored the shared cause once so large families of assertions flipped together (matching anchor 8). It fixed generators of failures rather than instances. It falls short of 10 because of minor semantic flip-flopping (trap-message thrashing) and no demonstrable updating of plans/milestones to reflect new understanding.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
